candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care: document client care accurately, maintain legal/professional accountability, communicate changes and interventions, and follow organizational/regulatory requirements for records.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — legal nursing documentation and record correction
candidate.educational_objective: Document nursing assessments, interventions, communications, and client responses accurately and promptly after care, and correct charting errors through a traceable approved process without deleting or concealing the original record.

options.A: Document assessments and care objectively, accurately, and promptly after they occur, and correct errors through the approved traceable record process.
options.B: Document planned interventions before they are performed when the nurse expects to complete them by the end of the shift.
options.C: Delete an inaccurate electronic entry so the original information is no longer visible in the record.
options.D: Limit documentation to medications and procedures because client assessments and responses are not part of the legal health record.

candidate.rationale: Current Open RN/NCBI nursing guidance states that the electronic health record is a legal document and that nursing documentation should be objective, factual, professional, accurate, and timely. Care or assessments that were not completed must never be charted as completed, and documentation should occur after the task or as close to the time of care as possible. Electronic charting errors should be corrected using the record's traceable correction process rather than erased or concealed. Therefore A is correct. B is advance/falsified charting, C destroys the audit trail, and D incorrectly excludes assessments and responses from nursing documentation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Nursing documentation is part of the legal health record and must be objective, accurate, timely, completed after care, and corrected through a traceable process rather than erased or prospectively falsified.
candidate.source_document_title: Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition — Communication: Documentation; Nursing Management and Professional Concepts — Legal Implications
